bundle: WI-7 / L-038 — Marico Limited debt-component completeness
workItem: IIPS v3.0 IID — L-038 resolution attempt, continuation of WI-7 (Consumer / Marico Limited)
question: The enterprise-to-equity bridge needs four borrowing components — short-term borrowings, current maturities of long-term debt, long-term borrowings and lease liabilities — at one balance-sheet instant. WI-7 recorded that Marico's consolidated statements print no current-maturity line anywhere. Does the filing in fact support a complete, period-aligned breakdown, and if it does, can gross debt, net debt and the enterprise-to-equity bridge be computed on the existing governed path without inferring anything?
answer: The caption exists and WI-7 missed it: Note 13(a) prints a 'scheduled maturity of long term borrowings' table whose first row is exactly 'Within one year (Current maturities of long term debt)', in both reports and for every period column. But the row carries a dash for FY2024 and FY2022 and a printed 0 only for FY2023, and the non-current borrowings row is a dash for FY2024. So the FY2024 component set — the period the valuation needs — is two dashes short, the FY2023 set is complete but belongs to a different balance-sheet instant, and the governed contract (rightly) refuses to mix them. Gross debt and net debt therefore still cannot be published, and L-038 stays OPEN. One dataset cell was corrected (FY2023 current maturities = the printed 0) so the record no longer asserts an absence the filing does not have; the refusal now names the real obstacle (PERIOD_MISMATCH across 2024-03-31 and 2023-03-31) instead of 'not reported'.
governingRule: D-2 and L-040: unavailable inputs must remain unavailable; they must never silently become zero and produce an apparently valid valuation. A dash is neither a number nor a declaration (register §17.14); a printed zero is a reported amount (ingestion builder: 'a reported zero is PRESENT with a source'); a declared nil requires the filer's quoted wording.

outcome.mappingAppliedDetail: one dataset cell: FY2023 CURRENT_MATURITIES_OF_LONG_TERM_DEBT = 0 (printed in both reports' scheduled-maturity tables)
outcome.reason: No complete, period-aligned set of the four debt components exists for 2024-03-31, which is the balance-sheet instant the valuation runs on: non-current borrowings and current maturities are both printed as dashes there. A complete set exists only for 2023-03-31, and the governed aggregation refuses to mix balance-sheet instants (PERIOD_MISMATCH). Nothing was inferred from totals, prior periods or arithmetic residuals. A second, independent blocker sits behind it: preference capital is NOT_REPORTED (authorised preference shares exist, issued preference shares are not printed and are not declared nil), so the enterprise-to-equity conversion would refuse even with a closed debt side.

l040Finding.what: The WI-7 payload — the artifact this bundle supersedes — publishes nine per-share sensitivity cells (107.95 to 187.23) computed with net debt, preference capital and associates/JV substituted as zero, because it was built by the code that existed before the L-040 correction. The corrected code publishes no per-share cell there.
l040Finding.evidence: runs/04-payload-diff.json lists the nine `value -> null` cells each gaining a diagnostic `enterpriseValue`; the arithmetic is exactly (EV - NCI) / shares with the three unavailable terms at zero
l040Finding.statusEffect: none — L-040 stays RESOLVED; the defect is in the artifact, not in the shipped code. The WI-7 payload is preserved byte-identical as historical evidence and is marked superseded for two independent reasons: the corrected FY2023 dataset cell, and the pre-correction grid
l040Finding.whyItMatters: it is the first time an earlier bundle's payload has been found to carry an already-corrected defect; the register entry records it so the superseded artifact cannot be read as the shipped behaviour

contractQuestion.question: When every debt component is disclosed but not at one balance-sheet instant, the contract refuses with PERIOD_MISMATCH and the payload can name only one reason. Should the contract (a) permit a bridge built entirely on the newest instant at which all four components carry numbers, here 2023-03-31 — at which gross debt is 608 crore (2 + 473 + 0 + 133) against cash and current investments of 785 crore (207 + 578), i.e. net debt -177 crore — and if so, must the cash side and the valuation's own inputs move with it; or (b) keep refusing, on the ground that a valuation dated 2024-03-31 cannot use 2023 borrowings?
contractQuestion.whyNotDecidedHere: either answer changes what the bridge may do with a filing's disclosed figures; it is a valuation-contract decision for the register owner, not an evidence question. It is deliberately left undecided, and the aggregation code was not touched.
contractQuestion.distinctFrom: L-039's cash-side nil-propagation finding, which is untouched by this work item

reconciliation.note: same instant, governed definitions on both sides: 608 - 785 = -177

payloadCashAndInvestments.note: the payload's cash side is a 2024-03-31 amount; 608 - 487 = +121 crore subtracts a 2024 balance from a 2023 one and is not a net-debt figure at any date

reconciliation.correctsEarlierWording: an earlier revision of the register, tracker, report and this determination quoted the 608 / -177 pair without the 785 crore cash figure, which read as inconsistent with the published 487 crore

whatWouldCloseL038: a filing that prints an amount (or a zero) for non-current borrowings AND current maturities at the valuation's balance-sheet instant — the ordinary route and the only purely evidentiary one, OR
a filing that declares either of them nil in its own words, which D-2 can record as NIL_BY_DISCLOSURE, OR
a register-owner decision on DEBT-COMPONENT-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT (above), which would let a complete older-period set be used — a contract decision this work item does not take, OR
a register-owner decision to give a filed dash a governed grade (the first option named in register §17.15), which would make the FY2024 dashes usable without pretending they are numbers

verification.readback: runs/03-readback.json — separate process, digest match true

secondBlocker.why: the enterprise-to-equity conversion requires preference capital to be a number or a declared nil; it is neither. A closed debt side would therefore still not have produced a per-share value. Recorded so the blocker is not mistaken for a single one.

cashSideAlignment.observation: capitalStructure.ts enforces the same-instant rule among the four debt components only (grossDebtOf, line 121). The cash side is cashAndInvestments = sum([cash, currentInvestments]) (line 224) and netDebt = subtract(grossDebt, cashAndInvestments) (line 225), with no comparison of the cash periods against the debt periods.
cashSideAlignment.whyItMattersHere: On Marico the path is never reached: grossDebt is NOT_COMPUTABLE, so subtract() returns the blocked minuend and no net-debt number is published. But if DEBT-COMPONENT-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT were granted as originally worded, the published net debt would be 608 - 487 = +121 crore, the 2024 cash side against the 2023 debt side — the cross-period arithmetic the bridge exists to refuse.
cashSideAlignment.notActedOn: no aggregation code, policy, dataset value, payload or period-alignment rule was changed; the finding is recorded only
cashSideAlignment.distinctFrom: L-039 (cash-side nil propagation), which is untouched
